newsitem.title: UK: Strong pound could push Britain into recession-study.
newsitem.headline: Strong pound could push Britain into recession-study.

text.p: Britain could be forced into recession within two years if the pound, which has soared in value by around 25 percent in the past year, remains strong, according to a study to be released on Thursday.

Cambridge Econometrics, a private forecasting company, said it had run computer models to establish what would happen to British industry if the pound's value averaged 2.80 deutschemarks over the next three years instead of undergoing an orderly depreciation.
"Under this scenario, consumers' expenditure growth remains strong in 1998 and then falls back sharply in 1999 as the terms of trade benefits wear off," the company said.

"UK GDP growth is slightly higher in 1997 but then lower than the base case thereafter as the unfavourable trade effects offset the boost from higher consumer spending. A recession would probably be precipitated by 1999."
Sterling was trading at around 3.0 deutschemarks on Wednesday, below its recent highs.

Cambridge Econometrics said that although manufacturing would be hardest hit by continued pound strength, the hitherto buoyant services sector would also be affected. If the pound remained strong over the next three years, gross domestic product would be around two percent lower than it would be if the currency staged an orderly retreat.
All regions of Britain would suffer but Scotland and Wales would experience the sharpest slowdown.
